subject: summary.fitted.values has less rows than observed data

messages.author: 78f18e5a32647f45
messages.subject: summary.fitted.values has less rows than observed data
parts:
Dear inla community

I'm trying to fit a survival model with three linear covariates and a bym spatial random effect. I first structured my data using inla.surv and inla.coxph and then updated the model with spatial random effect in inla function. I used the standard k = 15, so for i = 156 units I thought I will have 156*15 = 2340 rows in the summary.fitted.values. Unfortunately, this is not the case, I always have less fitted values than my original data. When I look deeper into the fitted values, I notice that after k=4 I always have fewer fitted values than the number of areas in the dataset (i=156). Is there any explanation for this? If this is not normal, how should I fix it? In the attachment, you find the code and data I used.

Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Yessika

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] summary.fitted.values has less rows than observed data
parts:
when you do 'inla.coxph' then its expanded into poisson regression, but the dimension of the model will depends on the data, as the expansion depends on it. this is why you get different dimensions in each fit.

looking at your code, it seems like you can benefite from having the baseline hazard defined on fixed intervals so you can more easily compare them, so I added



cut.points <- 1:30



and then use these 'cut.points' to define the baseline hazard


res.10 <- inla.coxph(inla.10 ~ 1 + time_std + inc_10_rate + as.factor(idzone),
data = c(list(inla.10 = inla.10, data0)),
control.hazard = list(cutpoints = cut.points))

res[[i]] <- inla(update(res.10$formula,
'. ~ . + f(idarea1, model = "bym2", graph = gFULL)'),


please use 'bym2' instead as it do automatically the right thing.


please check model/data as it seems that the information you have in the data is not to much for the model you have. maybe you want to merge it all and do the space-time model?

Best
H

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] summary.fitted.values has less rows than observed data
parts:
the automatic set changepoints are fine usually, but when you are to
compare for every year, you may want to have the same changepoints for
every year, hence you can set them upfront.

I just noticed that the marginal stdev's were large, which is either
because of confounding in the model , or to complex model for the data
you have...

Best
H
